claim: Children go from below chance to above chance on verbal false-belief tasks between about 41 and 48 months, across 178 studies; age alone explains R2=.39 of primary conditions, odds rise 2.94 per year. This curve does not choose between simulation and theory. Gap search: a 2026 preregistered cross-cultural study (Namibia, Germany; abstract only) finds task format matters for one group.
agent_test: none (background); use as human norm in eval design
audit_note: SEP merely cites Wellman 2001 so the numbers rest on one meta-analysis; the 2026 Namibia/Germany gap-search study is not in the listed sources and was not checked; Wellman's authors themselves read the curve as favouring theory-theory.

claim: Preregistered replications of anticipatory-looking false-belief tasks in 2-year-olds failed (Kampis 160 infants, only 54% of 90 analysed anticipated even in the control trial; Schuwerk 2018 N=48 and N=78 failed, adults N=115 passed). Implicit infant belief tracking from one paradigm is not established. Gap search: Kulke 2018 replicated 1 of 4 anticipatory-looking paradigms and that one failed without confounds (abstract only); a looking-time communication study (Song 2008) replicated only with a closer procedure and also showed the effect for uninformative statements (OSF abstract only). Onishi and Baillargeon 2005 itself still unchecked.
agent_test: Never score belief tracking with one paradigm; use at least 2 formats
audit_note: Kampis PMC and PubMed lines are one paper (Schuwerk is the independent second); Kulke 2018, Song 2008 and Onishi 2005 parts were not in the opened sources; 54% is of the 90 analysed in the second familiarization trial.

claim: Classic false-belief items are solved by strong LLMs (Kosinski: GPT-4 75% of 40 tasks with all controls, GPT-3.5 20%, davinci-002 5%), but scores depend on strict scoring: davinci-003 fell 90 to 20% when true-belief controls were added.
agent_test: Pair each false-belief item with a true-belief control; report strict all-pass score
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Adversarial or trivially altered false-belief items break LLMs that pass the classic version (Ullman GPT-3.5; Shapira GPT-4 transparent-access 0%). Humans also fail about half of such perturbations (Strachan N=757), so perturbation failure is not clean evidence of no ToM.
agent_test: Run each belief step on original plus perturbed variants at equal tokens; compare to a human baseline where available

claim: Some apparent LLM ToM failures are response bias, not inference failure: GPT faux-pas failure was hyperconservatism (Strachan); o1-preview scores 100 false-belief but 36 true-belief (ThoughtTracing), i.e. it over-suspects false belief. Strachan confirms: GPT faux-pas failure is hyperconservatism, LLaMA2 lead is ignorance bias (opened).
agent_test: Score both false- and true-belief items; flag asymmetric accuracy
audit_note: Strachan is listed twice (PMC and Nature are one paper); 'over-suspects false belief' is an interpretation of the 100 vs 36 split, which the paper frames as the model wrongly inferring the agent did not witness the event.

claim: A two-call simulation-style prompt (SimToM: filter story to what the character knows, then answer) raises false-belief accuracy for weaker models: GPT-3.5 BigToM FB 41.0 to 70.5 (+29.5), ToMI 67.25 to 81.0; Llama2-7b 47.5 to 70.5. For GPT-4 BigToM the gain is small or mixed (89.0 0-shot, 93.25 CoT, 92.0 SimToM). Verified against Table 1. Gap search: an independent lab (Chen 2026, 2025 backbones, about 200 items per cell) finds SimToM below plain inference on BigToM belief accuracy (Qwen3-32B 0.355 vs 0.900) but above it on SimpleToM action accuracy (Llama-3-8B 0.900 vs 0.505). No longer safe to call a general gain.
agent_test: Implement filter as a separate call vs one prompt; compare at equal tokens against CoT on BigToM and ToMI

claim: SimToM depends on keeping the filter as a separate call and on filter quality: single-prompt version loses about 20 points (GPT-3.5 BigToM FB 70.5 to 50.75), oracle perspectives give 96 on both benchmarks. Only GPT-3.5 ablated, one paper. Gap search: OmniToM finds model-written belief extraction tops out near F1 0.62, consistent with filter quality limiting the gain.
agent_test: Test filter quality separately; measure oracle-filter upper bound on own items

claim: SimToM gains do not generalise to harder benchmarks or multi-agent settings: on MMToM-QA GPT-4 goes 48.0 to 52.5 (false-belief 12 to 15), and on UniToMBench it hurt Llama3-8B and Gemma2-27B on evolving stories by giving all agents the same knowledge. Gap search: independent runs agree that SimToM gains do not transfer reliably.
agent_test: Check the filter on multi-agent items where agents differ in knowledge
audit_note: MMToM-QA 48.0->52.5 and false-belief 12->15 verified; UniToMBench text attributes the 'all agents share same knowledge' behaviour to its TOMBENCH tasks while evolving-story declines are described as failing to track belief updates; UniToMBench is not a harder benchmark in itself, and 'gap search' rests on Chen 2026 Table 2 (SimToM below plain inference on several belief rows, but higher on SimpleToM action accuracy).

claim: Explicit belief tracking or a theory-style generative model beats prompting alone on harder ToM: SymbolicToM gives GPT-4 +4 to +42 on ToMi; MMToM-QA text GPT-4 48.0, SymbolicToM 63.0, BIP-ALM 71.7 (multimodal 75.3-76.7 vs GPT-4V 44.0); false-belief item 12.0 vs 61-69. Verified against Table 1.
agent_test: Keep a code-held who-knows-what ledger and have the model answer over the filtered view; compare to prompt-only
audit_note: Only two distinct papers (Jin 2024, Sclar 2023); BIP-ALM text-only is 71.7 with GPT-J but 70.5 with LLaMA 2, and SymbolicToM scored 0.0 on goal type 2.3, so the advantage is not uniform.

claim: Inference-time hypothesis generation and weighting about another party's mental state helps: ThoughtTracing on GPT-4o ParaphrasedToMi 59.5 to 76.0, FANToM AllQs 11.1 to 41.5 (54.7 with CoT), MMToM avg 56.5 to 60.0 (goal sub-score fell 56.1 to 37.8); Hypothetical Minds scored hypotheses by predictive success in Melting Pot. Gains uneven across models and subtasks.
agent_test: Keep a scored hypothesis list about the other party, updated from outcomes; test equal-token vs CoT
audit_note: The goal sub-score drop 56.1 to 37.8 is CoT versus TT (plain GPT-4o was 39.8); wording is ambiguous. ThoughtTracing numbers match Table; Hypothetical Minds abstract confirms hypothesis scoring in Melting Pot.

claim: LLMs infer who knows what but fail to apply it to behaviour: SimpleToM mental state above 95%, behaviour prediction GPT-4o 49.5 and Claude-3.5-Sonnet 67.0, judgment 10 to 25. Putting the model's own earlier awareness answer back in the prompt raises behaviour to 82.8 and 96.9; a generic system prompt does nothing and generic CoT helps only partly (GPT-4o 49.5 to 62.8, Claude 67.0 to 77.2). Riemer et al. show the same gap in repeated games, even with oracle inputs.
schema_part: S/O (code passes inferred belief into next step)
agent_test: Code inserts a 'what does X know' line before the action question; measure behaviour accuracy at equal tokens
audit_note: Table 3 verified (82.8, 96.9, 49.5, 67.0), but generic CoT is not 'little': it raised behaviour prediction from 49.5 to 62.8 (GPT-4o) and 67.0 to 77.2 (Claude) and judgment 15.3 to 39.2 (GPT-4o); only the generic system prompt was flat.
claim_before_audit: LLMs infer who knows what but fail to apply it to behaviour: SimpleToM mental state above 95%, behaviour prediction GPT-4o 49.5, Claude-3.5-Sonnet 67.0, judgment 10 to 25. Putting the model's own earlier awareness answer back in the prompt raises behaviour to 82.8 and 96.9; generic system prompt and generic CoT help little. Verified against Table 3. Gap search: Riemer shows the same gap in repeated games, even with oracle inputs.

claim: Consistency across question types about the same hidden fact exposes illusory ToM: FANToM ALL score human 87.5, GPT-4 CoT 26.6 and 14.8 across two runs, ChatGPT 3.7; fine-tuned Flan-T5 53.7.
agent_test: Evaluate with multi-question consistency, not single accuracy
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Models anchor on the story-stated state and fail most at backward belief inference from an action: BigToM backward belief humans 82/72%, GPT-4 0-shot .53 false-belief, many models below chance.
agent_test: Include backward-inference items (infer what a user wants from their actions) in agent eval
audit_note: Numbers rest on one paper (BigToM listed twice); Zhu et al. does not report the human/GPT-4 figures; the paper ties anchoring on a stated belief to forward belief inference and says backward errors are worse especially with an explicit initial belief.

claim: Interpretability studies find separate decodable self and other belief representations (Zhu 2024) and a linear map to a first-person view that weakly flips answers (Aoki 2025, 198/200 and 196/200 kept items, small flip rate). Weak and mechanistic only; it does not show simulation beats theory. Gap search: Zhu steering row mapping still inferred from garbled table.
agent_test: Not testable at the prompt level; skip unless interpretability is available

claim: Whether LLM ToM is theory-like is contested: GPT-4o shows human-like belief-desire-cost predictions in one domain but cross-domain consistency is low (beliefs rho .78, desires .39, costs .18); Lombardi and Lenci find actions often not chosen from attributed beliefs.
agent_test: Check cross-domain consistency of inferred mental states for the agent

claim: Adult humans egocentrically anchor and under-adjust when simulating others (Epley et al. 2004; curse of knowledge, per SEP), which simulation theory explains as failing to quarantine one's own knowledge. Executive function is moderately linked to false-belief understanding in children (102 studies, 9,994 children; Devine and Hughes 2014). Whether LLMs show the same leak is not shown by these sources. One 2026 preprint finds first-person versus third-person framing changes recovered belief structure (single model, other domain).
schema_part: O (role-taking operator with explicit separation of own vs other knowledge)
agent_test: Compare one-pass vs multi-pass adjustment of role-taking at equal tokens
audit_note: Epley 2004 and Devine & Hughes 2014 check out (Devine concerns EF broadly, not specifically inhibition), but none of the opened sources shows that LLMs show the same egocentric leak; that sentence is unsupported.
claim_before_audit: Adult humans egocentrically anchor and under-adjust when simulating others (Epley 2004; curse of knowledge); LLMs show the same leak, which is the rationale for quarantining own knowledge. Executive function (inhibition) links to false belief in children (102 studies, 9,994 children). Gap search: first-person vs third-person framing changes recovered belief structure (single model, other domain), CoT does not.

claim: Child ToM training works (g=0.75, 45 studies, 1,529 children) and language ability predicts false belief (104 studies, N=8,891), supporting an explicit-concepts reading, but neither separates simulation from theory.
agent_test: Add explicit mental-state concept rules vs perspective only; compare
audit_note: Both are correlational/training meta-analyses; 'supporting an explicit-concepts reading' is the researcher's interpretation, not either paper's claim.

claim: Simulation and theory accounts have converged on hybrids; mirror and mentalizing systems in over 200 fMRI studies split by input type (concrete actions vs abstract stories), so no single account is established.
agent_test: Use explicit rules for facts, role-taking for what someone would conclude; test hybrid vs either alone

claim: Higher-order belief depth: GPT-4 matches adults on orders 2-6 true/false statements (order 2 100% vs 96%), but Hi-ToM accuracy falls to near zero at order 4 and CoT adds little (GPT-4 58.11 vs 59.88). Sources disagree on whether depth is a weak point (different formats).
agent_test: Test nesting depth 2-4 on own items with and without a belief ledger

claim: Static ToM benchmarks may not measure functional ToM: in Riemer et al.'s repeated games, essentially no LLM matched a tabular frequency-count baseline on regret (one inconsistent exception, CoT Mistral Large 2 on Iterated Battle of Sexes), and ToMBench finds the best LLM (GPT-4-1106) about 10 points under humans overall (75.3 vs 85.4) while exceeding humans on the false-belief task.
agent_test: Evaluate adaptation to a partner across turns, not one-shot questions
audit_note: Riemer appendix reports one exception (CoT Mistral Large 2 on Iterated Battle of Sexes beat RMax with 3 examples, but is inconsistent and fails on RPS); ToMBench says LLMs like GPT-4-1106 outperform humans on the false-belief task but does not say that is the only task.
claim_before_audit: Static ToM benchmarks may not measure functional ToM: no LLM beat a frequency-count baseline in repeated-game adaptation (Riemer), and ToMBench shows GPT-4 beating humans only on false belief while about 10 points under overall.

claim: Reasoning models do not reliably beat non-reasoning models on ToM, and more thinking hurts on hard higher-order items: o3 HiToM 0.838 at low effort to 0.693 at high; on ToMATO the non-reasoning twin wins in all pairings (Qwen3-8B 0.705 vs 0.648). A moderate CoT or a token cap helps (Qwen3-8B reasoning capped at 1,500 tokens 0.706). Removing answer options lifts R1 from 0.549 to 0.691, so part of the score is option matching.
agent_test: Compare capped vs uncapped thinking per ToM step; score free-form, not multiple choice

claim: A model-written ledger of who knows what is unreliable: best Stage 1 belief-extraction F1 is 61.63 (Gemini-2.5 Pro), knowledge-access labelling 56-75% across models, and extraction rank differs from endpoint QA rank (Gemma-3 27B second vs ninth).
agent_test: Cross-check ledger entries by code or a second pass before using them

claim: A scored hypothesis list about another agent (Hypothetical Minds) beats ReAct, PlanReAct and Reflexion in multi-agent games; scoring plus refinement is the active part; top_k above 3 gives diminishing returns. It uses 3+k calls per step and costs more than PlanReAct ($4); no token-matched comparison exists.
agent_test: Run with a token budget equal to best-of-N

claim: In an interactive card game, first-order ToM tracks success more than second-order ToM (r=0.76 vs 0.58, about 14 models, LLM-judge scored).
agent_test: Prioritise reliable first-order tracking over deep nesting

claim: Benchmark scores can be reached without human-like simulation: 7B RL-trained model gets Hi-ToM 84.50% vs GPT-4o 69.00%, with collapsed short reasoning in 3B models; SFT matches RL. Template benchmarks are weak evidence for simulation or theory.
agent_test: Use held-out item structure and process checks
